stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion as it focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness. The Department of Defense's interest in such capabilities is evident, as military contracts increasingly drive funding in this sector. This cash infusion could accelerate its development timeline significantly.
stories.soWhat: With DoD backing, True Anomaly is positioned to capitalize on increasing military demand for space security solutions—because who doesn't want their satellites to be less vulnerable?

stories.head: Commerce Department moves on mission authorization system
stories.body: The Office of Space Commerce is advancing a voluntary mission authorization system for unregulated space activities, which could reshape how companies approach compliance in the expanding space economy. This move comes amid growing concerns about space traffic management and safety, reflecting a shift towards self-regulation in the industry.
stories.soWhat: If companies don’t get their act together, the government might just do it for them—welcome to the new era of space governance.

stories.head: China's Long March 3B defies lightning to launch satellites
stories.body: Despite being struck by lightning shortly after liftoff, China's Long March 3B successfully deployed five satellites, showcasing the resilience of its launch capabilities. This incident raises questions about launch reliability and safety protocols in extreme conditions, particularly as China ramps up its space ambitions.
stories.soWhat: If lightning can’t stop a rocket, one has to wonder what it takes to ground the competition—perhaps a little more than a thunderstorm.

watchlist.title: Watch for more AI in defense contracts
watchlist.body: As the trend of 'AI for Defense' accelerates, expect more startups to pivot towards this lucrative sector, potentially reshaping the competitive landscape.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's timeline for Dream Chaser
watchlist.body: With its DoD variant passing critical design review, the clock is ticking for Sierra Space to deliver on its promises—investors will be watching closely.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension implications
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension suggests the government is doubling down on ground station capabilities, which could set a precedent for future contracts.

watchlist.title: Kinetica-1's next launch plans
watchlist.body: Following its successful launch, Kinetica-1 may ramp up its schedule, making it a player to watch in the small satellite market.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
